claim: Regional Data Transfer rates apply to traffic between EC2 instances when the other instance is in a different Availability Zone, whatever address type is used, or when public or Elastic IP addresses are used, whichever Availability Zone the other instance is in; you are charged only once for a given instance even if both are true.
question: Is traffic between EC2 instances over public or Elastic IP addresses charged even inside one Availability Zone, and is cross-AZ traffic over public IPs charged twice?

values.display: Public or Elastic IP addresses are used, regardless of which Availability Zone the other instance is in
values.spoken: public or Elastic IP addresses cost Regional data transfer, even in the same zone

values.display: The other instance is in a different Availability Zone, regardless of which type of address is used
values.spoken: a different Availability Zone costs Regional data transfer, whatever the address

values.display: you are only charged once for a given instance even if both are true

qualifiers.scope: per GB between EC2 instances in one Region
qualifiers.condition: Regional Data Transfer rates; the rate itself is on the EC2 pricing page

evidence.quote: Regional Data Transfer rates apply if at least one of the following is true, but you are only charged once for a given instance even if both are true:
The other instance is in a different Availability Zone, regardless of which type of address is used.
Public or Elastic IP addresses are used, regardless of which Availability Zone the other instance is in.

note: Added by the chapter 10 registrar for demand items d007 and d124 (targeted search of the EC2 FAQ). Teaching point: use private IP addresses inside a Region to avoid Regional Data Transfer charges in the same Availability Zone.
